name: Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc.
sector: Industrials / Water management — stormwater & wastewater products
moat_justification: Moderate-strong moat: North America's leading stormwater manager with scale in corrugated HDPE pipe, a dense local plant/distribution network that gives a freight-cost advantage on bulky pipe rivals cannot replicate, Infiltrator's dominant plastic leachfield-chamber position, spec/code approvals and one of the largest plastic-recycling operations (resin cost integration). Evidence: ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) 17.6% / 16.3% / 29.3% / 28.8% / 21.5% over FY2021–FY2025 — well above the cost of capital through a resin-price cycle — easing to 14.5% in FY2026 as the ~$991M NDS acquisition (closed Feb 2026) inflated invested capital ahead of its earnings contribution; gross margin recovered from the FY2022 resin squeeze (28.9%) to 36.4–39.9% in FY2023–FY2026 (38.6% TTM), proving pricing power with a lag. Capped at 6 because the core pipe product is close to commodity (JM Eagle, Lane Enterprises, concrete/steel substitutes), resin and freight costs squeeze margins before price actions catch up (FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin guided down ~170–200bp), and demand is construction-cyclical. CAP = 9.8 years.
fragility_flags: BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.6%) vs bull-case tier C (10.8%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality stormwater franchise, moat 6/10 with ROIC 16–29% through the cycle — but at $127.78 the OE yield is only 4.97% and weighted IRR is 8.80% (IV@15% $62.23); it clears 15% only below ~$62, and even the super-bull case (14.88%) stays under the hurdle.
moat_for: #1 North American stormwater position — scale in corrugated HDPE pipe and the broadest water-management product line (pipe, chambers, Infiltrator, NDS, Orenco)
Dense network of 60+ local plants and distribution — freight is the binding cost on bulky low-value-density pipe, so local scale is a structural cost advantage smaller rivals cannot match
ROIC proxy 16–29% across FY2021–FY2025 and gross margin rebuilt to ~38–40% after the FY2022 resin squeeze — pricing power proven, with a lag
Spec-in / code-approval position and Infiltrator's dominant share of plastic leachfield chambers — engineers and distributors default to ADS systems
Vertical integration into recycled resin (one of North America's largest plastic recyclers) — input-cost and supply advantage vs virgin-resin buyers
moat_against: Core corrugated pipe is near-commodity: JM Eagle, Lane Enterprises and regional makers plus concrete/steel pipe substitution contest every bid
Resin and transportation cost inflation compresses margins before pricing catches up — FY2022 gross margin fell to 28.9% and FY2027 EBITDA margin is guided down ~170–200bp on resin/freight
Construction cyclicality: revenue fell in FY2024 (-6.4%) and OE/share ranged from $1.39 (FY2022) to $6.85 (FY2026) over five years
Growth increasingly bought: NDS (~$991M, Feb 2026) and Orenco ($237M, FY2025) add goodwill, integration risk and debt — net debt $1,388.8M, 2.79x normalized OE
No recurring-revenue or contractual lock-in — every project is re-bid; the moat is cost/spec position, not switching costs on installed product
